description: Bring the primary operator workflows to the web first: gains tracking, 1099-B export, FIFO sale forecasting, and explicit wallet-separated tax handling for 2025+ IRS rules.

timing.gatingCondition: Proceed after Feature-17 establishes JSON contracts and authenticated API baseline.

principles: Tax First - prioritize the workflows that motivated the product
Wallet Separation Is Core - per-wallet accounting is a first-class requirement, not a warning banner afterthought
Explain The Lots - expose lot-level reasoning so forecast results remain auditable
CSV Still Matters - exported files must remain practical for downstream tax tooling
Parity With Existing Core - web results must match current Python calculations exactly

techStack.frontend: Web UI consuming Python JSON endpoints
techStack.testing: pytest API tests + fixture-driven equivalence tests against existing calculator outputs

userStories.title: Web gains tracker endpoints and UI
acceptanceCriteria: Expose gains tracker endpoint returning summary metrics and lot-by-lot worksheet data
Support filters for tax year, coin, and wallet
Render a phone-friendly gains summary view with drill-in on desktop
Match existing FIFO calculations from the Python core exactly
userStories.testStrategy: pytest tax endpoint equivalence tests against known fixtures

userStories.title: Wallet-separated 1099-B export workflow
acceptanceCriteria: Expose authenticated API to preview and export 1099-B data
Require explicit wallet selection for tax year 2025 and beyond by default
Show clear operator guidance when a pre-2025 global FIFO export is requested
Preserve CSV shape suitable for existing downstream usage
userStories.testStrategy: pytest export route tests and CSV snapshot assertions

userStories.title: Hypothetical sale forecasting for mobile and desktop
acceptanceCriteria: Expose forecast endpoint returning lots consumed, short-term vs long-term splits, and proceeds/cost basis summaries
Provide concise mobile summary and deeper desktop lot table from the same endpoint
Allow wallet-filtered forecasts for per-wallet tax planning
Handle missing basis explicitly in both API and UI
userStories.testStrategy: pytest forecast endpoint tests with wallet-scoped scenarios

userStories.title: Tax policy guidance and operator warnings
acceptanceCriteria: Show 2025+ wallet-separation guidance prominently in the web flow
Differentiate compliant wallet-scoped flows from convenience-only historical flows
Provide links or inline notes to repo guidance on IRS wallet rules
Do not silently produce ambiguous exports
userStories.testStrategy: UI smoke tests + manual review of warning conditions

userStories.title: Saved tax presets and recent export history
acceptanceCriteria: Allow saving common export/filter presets for the primary user
Show recent forecast and export runs for quick recall from phone
Persist lightweight metadata without duplicating the underlying tax computation outputs
Keep implementation private-user simple; no multi-user sharing model required
userStories.testStrategy: pytest preset persistence tests + API round-trip checks

high: Any divergence from the existing Python tax logic would undermine the purpose of the web port
Weak handling of 2025+ wallet separation would create operator confusion at the most important workflow
medium: Mobile layout may hide too much lot detail unless drill-downs are designed intentionally
CSV expectations may be stricter than a pure web-preview implementation first assumes
low: The underlying calculator APIs already exist and are exercised by tests
Tax/reporting flows are self-contained enough to ship before imports

preFlightChecklist: Confirm whether wallet selection should be hard-required or overrideable for 2025+ exports
Identify current CSV consumers and preserve required column shapes
Choose how recent export history should be stored
Confirm mobile-first summary metrics that matter most during routine use
